## Quarto

Quarto enables you to weave together content and executable code into a finished document. To learn more about Quarto see <https://quarto.org>.

## Running Code

When you click the **Render** button a document will be generated that includes both content and the output of embedded code. You can embed code like this:

```{r}
1 + 1
```

You can add options to executable code like this

```{r}
#| echo: false
2 * 2
```

The `echo: false` option disables the printing of code (only output is displayed).

way to filter out some data: drop people who don’t have a college major coded (including all the people who didn’t get a college degree)

```{r}
acs_coll <- acs2021 %>% filter(DEGFIELD != "N/A")
```

an even heavier filter: Which would be people between 25 and 55 (so-called prime age), who are in the labor force, working full year, usually fulltime, who are Hispanic females with a college degree. If you start from a really big dataset, then you can drill far down.

```{r}
acs_subgroup <- acs2021 %>% filter((AGE >= 25) & (AGE <= 55) & 
                                     (LABFORCE == 2) & 
                                     (WKSWORK2 > 4) & 
                                     (UHRSWORK >= 35) &
                                     (Hispanic == 1) & 
                                     (female == 1) & 
                                     ((educ_college == 1) | (educ_advdeg == 1)))
```

```{r}
table(DEGFIELDD)
```

```{r}
print(DEGFIELDD)
```

```{r}
compare_fields <- (   (acs2021$DEGFIELDD == "Civil Engineering") |
                        (acs2021$DEGFIELDD == "Electrical Engineering") |
                        (acs2021$DEGFIELDD == "Mechanical Engineering") |
                        (acs2021$DEGFIELDD == "Computer Science") | 
                        (acs2021$DEGFIELDD == "Psychology") |
                        (acs2021$DEGFIELDD == "Political Science and Government") |
                        (acs2021$DEGFIELDD == "Economics") |
                        (acs2021$EDUC == "Grade 12")  )

acs_compare_f <- acs2021 %>% filter((compare_fields & (AGE >= 25) & (AGE <= 65)) )

acs_compare_f$DEGFIELDD <- fct_drop(acs_compare_f$DEGFIELDD)


acs_compare_f$degree_recode <- recode_factor(acs_compare_f$DEGFIELDD, 
                                             "Economics" = "Econ",
                                             "Civil Engineering" = "Engr",
                                             "Electrical Engineering" = "Engr",
                                             "Mechanical Engineering" = "Engr",
                                             "Computer Science" = "CS",
                                             "Political Science and Government" = "PoliSci",
                                             "Psychology" = "Psych",
                                             .default = "HS")


p_age_income <- ggplot(data = acs_compare_f,
                       mapping = aes(x = AGE,
                                     y = INCWAGE,
                                     color = degree_recode,
                                     fill = degree_recode))

p_age_income + geom_smooth(aes(color=degree_recode, fill=degree_recode)) + 
  scale_color_viridis_d(option = "inferno", end = 0.85) + 
  scale_fill_viridis_d(option = "inferno", end = 0.65) + 
  labs(x = "Age", y = "Income",color = "field") + guides(fill = "none")
```

above is some code that shows the relationship of major to earnings, among majors offered here,

The transluscent parts are standard of error bands

```{r}
acs_compare_f$age_range <- cut(acs_compare_f$AGE, breaks = c(20.5, 30.5, 40.5, 50.5, 60.5, 70.5) )
levels(acs_compare_f$age_range) <- c("20s","30s","40s","50s","60s")

inc_by_agerange_degree <- acs_compare_f %>%
  group_by(age_range,degree_recode) %>%
  summarize(
    avg = mean(INCWAGE, na.rm = TRUE),
    stdev = sd(INCWAGE, na.rm = TRUE), 
    n_obs = n()
  ) 

kable(inc_by_agerange_degree)
```

```{r}
model <- lm(INCWAGE ~ AGE + I(AGE^2) + educ_college + female)
b <- coef(model)

peak_age <- -b["AGE"] / (2 * b["I(AGE^2)"])

# Predicted wage at peak age for each group
predict(model, newdata = data.frame(
  AGE = peak_age,
  educ_college = c(0, 1, 0, 1),
  female = c(0, 0, 1, 1)
))
```

```{r}
m_restricted <- lm(INCWAGE ~ AGE + I(AGE^2) + educ_college + female)

age_grid <- data.frame(AGE = 18:65, educ_college = 0, female = 0)
age_grid$quad    <- predict(m_restricted, age_grid)
age_grid$quartic <- predict(m_unrestricted, age_grid)

plot(age_grid$AGE, age_grid$quartic, type = "l", col = "red",
     xlab = "Age", ylab = "Predicted wage")
lines(age_grid$AGE, age_grid$quad)
legend("topleft", c("Quadratic", "Quartic"), col = c("black", "red"), lty = 1)

# Peak age under the quartic
age_grid$AGE[which.max(age_grid$quartic)]
```

```{r}
cps_pos <- subset(acs2021, !is.na(INCWAGE) & INCWAGE > 0)
model_log <- lm(log(INCWAGE) ~ AGE + I(AGE^2) + educ_college + female, data = cps_pos)
model_lvl <- lm(INCWAGE ~ AGE + I(AGE^2) + educ_college + female, data = cps_pos)
```

```{r}
library(ggplot2)

# Grid of ages x groups
grid <- expand.grid(AGE = 18:65, educ_college = c(0, 1), female = c(0, 1))

# Level model: predictions are already in dollars
grid$Level <- predict(model_lvl, newdata = grid)

# Log model: exponentiate, with Duan's smearing so it estimates the MEAN
smear <- mean(exp(residuals(model_log)))
grid$Log <- exp(predict(model_log, newdata = grid)) * smear

# Labels and long format for plotting
grid$group <- paste(ifelse(grid$female == 1, "Female", "Male"),
                    ifelse(grid$educ_college == 1, "College", "No college"),
                    sep = ", ")

grid_long <- reshape(grid, direction = "long",
                     varying = c("Level", "Log"), v.names = "pred",
                     timevar = "model", times = c("Level", "Log"))
```

```{r}
ggplot(grid_long, aes(AGE, pred, color = model, linetype = model)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  facet_wrap(~ group) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::dollar) +
  labs(title = "Predicted wage by age: level vs. log model",
       x = "Age", y = "Predicted wage", color = "Model", linetype = "Model") +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r}
obs <- aggregate(INCWAGE ~ AGE + educ_college + female, data = cps_pos, FUN = mean)
obs$group <- paste(ifelse(obs$female == 1, "Female", "Male"),
                   ifelse(obs$educ_college == 1, "College", "No college"), sep = ", ")
obs <- subset(obs, AGE %in% 18:65)

ggplot(grid_long, aes(AGE, pred, color = model)) +
  geom_point(data = obs, aes(AGE, INCWAGE), inherit.aes = FALSE,
             color = "grey50", alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  facet_wrap(~ group) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::dollar) +
  labs(title = "Predicted vs. observed mean wage by age",
       x = "Age", y = "Wage") +
  theme_minimal()
```
